title: Vector bundles and the tangent bundle
summary: Vector bundles via local trivialisations, transition functions and the cocycle condition; the tautological bundle over the Grassmannian; Whitney sums and pullbacks; tangent vectors as equivalence classes of chart–vector pairs and as derivations; the tangent bundle, coordinate vector fields and the differential of a smooth map; flows of vector fields.

objectives.description: Construct vector bundles from transition functions and verify the cocycle, pullback and Whitney-sum rules.
Identify tangent vectors through coordinates, curves and derivations, and show how the chain rule defines the tangent bundle.
Compute tangent and bundle maps while distinguishing local triviality from global triviality.

preparation.description: Read lecture 6: Definition 7.1 (vector bundle), Example 7.2 (tautological bundle), transition functions and the cocycle condition, §7.1 new bundles from old.
Read lecture 7 §7.2: Definition 7.3 (tangent vectors and the tangent bundle), coordinate vector fields, the differential Df and its Jacobian matrix.
Read Hitchin §3.2–3.3 (tangent and cotangent vectors, derivatives of smooth maps) and §4.1–4.3 (the tangent bundle, vector fields as derivations, flows).

activities.title: Lecture and exact source reading
activities.instructions: Work through the prepared lecture together with its named source sections. Reconstruct the displayed derivations before looking back. The source reading is part of this unit, including the proof obligations identified in the notes.

activities.instructions: Write an independent attempt at each problem. Use one hint at a time if needed; preserve the original attempt and record what assistance changed. Explain the hypotheses aloud before requesting a step check.

activities.title: Return without the scaffolding
activities.instructions: After a gap, reconstruct the central argument without notes and revisit the transfer or synthesis problem. Compare against your previous work only afterwards. Record what remains unresolved; reading or recall alone does not certify mastery.

exitCheck.description: Use the whole problem sheet to sample the listed objectives. Give an independent account of the main theorem and its hypotheses, and solve the transfer/synthesis task. An accepted single exercise is evidence only for its tested capabilities, not whole-unit mastery.

commonMisconceptions.claim: All rank-k bundles are the product with R^k because their fibres are isomorphic.
commonMisconceptions.correction: Bundle triviality requires one smoothly varying global frame. The Möbius bundle has isomorphic one-dimensional fibres but no nowhere-zero section.
